focus_areas.title: Clear Next Steps with the Right People
focus_areas.detail: After excellent discovery, the call ended with 'send me a summary' — an open loop with no date and no commitment. A document is not a next step; a meeting on the calendar is. This is the single biggest risk to the deal.
focus_areas.drill: I'll have that summary to you Thursday. Rather than you reading it cold, can we grab 30 minutes Friday so I can walk you and ideally your VP of Finance through it and the rough ROI? I'll send an invite for 2pm — does that work, or is morning better?

focus_areas.title: Booking the Meeting
focus_areas.detail: Ask for a specific time, not an email.
focus_areas.drill: 'How about we grab 15 minutes Wednesday at 10 so I can show you, rather than an email that gets buried?'

focus_areas.title: Interactivity & Comprehension Checks
focus_areas.drill: Pause: 'Before I go on — how does this compare to how you do it today?'

focus_areas.title: Clear Next Step into Post-Sale
focus_areas.drill: 'Let's get the pilot scoping on the calendar — does Thursday 2pm work?'

focus_areas.title: Decision Process & Stakeholders
focus_areas.detail: Jordan correctly identified that Finance and Operations own sign-off, then left it to Sam to 'feel it out.' Single-threaded deals stall. Make it easy and low-risk for Sam to bring them in now, while the pain is hot.
focus_areas.drill: Totally fair to socialize it first. To make that easy — want me to send a short, two-paragraph summary written for them, framed around the board-prep angle your Head of Ops has been pushing? Then if it resonates, the three of you join the Friday session. What's the best way to get on her radar?
